findings.description: The security group allows inbound TCP/22 from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH on the public instance to the entire internet and enabling brute-force or exploit attempts.
The egress rule permits all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, allowing a compromised instance unrestricted outbound access for data exfiltration or command-and-control.

The user_data script exports AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY in plaintext. EC2 user data is retrievable from the instance metadata service by anyone with access to the instance (including via SSRF), leaking long-lived AWS credentials.
No metadata_options block is set, so IMDSv1 remains enabled (http_tokens not 'required'), making instance credentials and the plaintext user_data reachable through SSRF attacks.
No root_block_device with encrypted = true is specified, so the root EBS volume may be unencrypted, leaving data at rest unprotected.
The instance is launched in a subnet with map_public_ip_on_launch = true routed to an internet gateway, giving it a public IP and direct internet exposure combined with an open SSH security group.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true (and no KMS key), so data written to the attached disk is stored unencrypted.
The snapshot is taken from an unencrypted volume, so the resulting snapshot is unencrypted and any accidental sharing would expose plaintext data.
The VPC flow log bucket has no server-side encryption configuration, so sensitive network telemetry is stored unencrypted.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block or ACL/policy restrictions are configured for the flow log bucket, risking accidental public exposure of network logs.
Versioning is not enabled and force_destroy = true permits deletion of a bucket containing audit/flow log data, undermining log integrity and tamper resistance.
No bucket policy enforces aws:SecureTransport, so flow log data could be transferred over unencrypted connections.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true causes every instance in this subnet to receive a public IP, automatically exposing workloads to the internet.

The VPC's default security group is not restricted via aws_default_security_group, so resources launched without an explicit group may inherit overly permissive default rules.
